title: In silico  DNA gyrase binding analysis of levofloxacin degradants: integrating DFT calculations, molecular docking, and dynamics simulation
content: Levofloxacin (Lev) is among the most widely used antibiotics, used to treat various bacterial infections by inhibiting bacterial DNA replication. However, the persistence of unmetabolized Lev residues or degradation products may raise public health and microbiome concerns due to their potential contribution to the development of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). This study investigates 16 Lev degradants formed through anaerobic, photolytic, photocatalytic, and acid hydrolysis. The density functional theory (DFT) at the B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) basis set was assigned for their geometry optimization, enabling further chemical and spectral analyses. Among them, most of the degradants showed a greater HOMO–LUMO energy gap than that of the parent molecule. Molecular docking was performed using bacterial DNA gyrase proteins from Escherichia coli and Streptococcus pneumoniae as targets and the degradants as ligands. The resulting protein–ligand complexes from docking underwent 100 ns of molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to assess their structural stability, flexibility, compactness, and interactions. The ADMET and PASS analyses of the degradants demonstrated altered biological and toxicological attributes, including mutagenicity, genotoxicity, DNA gyrase inhibition, and necrosis, compared to Lev. Our investigation provides vital toxicological predictions of Lev and its degradants and highlights the potential candidates for future studies.
